thread:
maya: FYI — Sequoia customer finetune (LoRA) merged into staging variant sequoia-lr-2026-03. Quick-eval pack sequoia-qe-202603 shows token-level swaps after ~3k tokens. attaching logs. :thinking:

alex: Can you paste a failing prompt/snippet? quick look would help.

maya: here's a minimal repro (trimmed):
```
Prompt: "Summarize the following transcript..."
Expected: "The meeting covered Q1 roadmap and infra upgrades."
Actual: "The meeting covered Q1 road and infraupgrades."  <-- tokens shifted, merging pieces of adjacent tokens
```

tariq: Hmmm, that looks like a tokenizer mismatch — are we accidentally mixing base tokenizer with customer tokenizer during the LoRA merge?

eva: I re-ran the merge locally with the merge tool: `./tools/merge_lora --base sequoia-base --lora sequoia-cust --out tmp` and reproduced. Dumped first 512 token ids for the prompt: `[10, 234, 45, 783, 9001, 12, 88, ...]` — when I load with base tokenizer they map differently.

alex: Try forcing the customer tokenizer: `tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('sequoia-cust-tokenizer', use_fast=False)` — when I decode ids with that tokenizer I get the expected spacing.

deploy-bot: perf-check: summary-bench shows BLEU drop ~0.7% on the customer's eval suite; latency and mem unchanged. (run id: run-2026-03-12-07)

maya: Plan: revert the merge on staging, add a tokenizer-mapping step into the merge tool to preserve token-id parity and add a quick-eval parity check for first 4k tokens in the CI pack. I'll open the revert + fix PR. @alex can you add the QE parity check to the sequoia-qe pack?

alex: On it. Drafting PR now — will include unit tests + end-to-end smoke. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/mergetool/pull/142

eva: Also suggest adding a small golden-diff artifact: `scripts/qe_report --pack sequoia-qe-202603 --diff > artifacts/sequoia-token-diff.txt` so we can track token mapping changes over time.

maya: Thanks all. reverting on staging and marking triaged :white_check_mark:
